claims.text: Trace Si doping enables dense consolidation of ZrB2 at approximately 1700 °C.
Si doping causes an Si-rich intergranular film to form in situ in ZrB2.
The Si-rich intergranular film evolves during oxidation into a silica-based or borosilicate phase.
The resulting silica-based or borosilicate phase is protective.
Trace Si enhances mass transport during sintering.
Trace Si improves grain-boundary bonding in ZrB2 at lower processing temperatures.
During high-temperature service, the Si-derived phase forms a continuous, self-healing oxide layer.
The Si-derived oxide layer increases the oxidation resistance of ZrB2.
The Si-derived oxide layer limits corrosion of ZrB2 by liquid plating metal.
Si-doped ZrB2 processed at approximately 1700 °C will have greater densification than undoped ZrB2 processed at the same temperature.
Si-doped ZrB2 will have mechanical strength and structural integrity comparable or superior to pure ZrB2 consolidated above 2300 °C.
Si-doped ZrB2 will resist oxidation at 1200–1500 °C better than both high-temperature-processed pure ZrB2 and lower-temperature undoped ZrB2.
Si-doped ZrB2 will have improved durability in liquid plating-metal environments relative to the stated pure and low-temperature undoped controls.
Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires processing above 2300 °C.
Undoped ZrB2 processed at approximately 1700 °C has compromised oxidation and liquid-metal corrosion resistance.
The intervention is applicable at sintering temperatures no greater than 1700 °C under an inert atmosphere.
The protective phase can provide useful service in oxidizing atmospheres up to approximately 1500 °C.
The protective phase can provide useful service in aggressive liquid-metal plating baths.
The starting material is single-phase ZrB2 powder without pre-existing secondary phases.
